name: Responsiveness

subjectOf.text: Traditional governance models lack the real time responsiveness to community sentiment that a decentralized WDAG system supplies, and this latency, not an absence of rules, is what leaves conventional AI governance out of step with community values.
subjectOf.abstract: The WDAG system's decentralized nature, which captures and integrates community sentiment and ethical considerations, provides a real-time responsiveness that is often lacking in traditional governance models.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, How AI Models are Optimized Through Web3 Governance (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4855607
scope_conditions: comparison of centralized governance models against decentralized, continuously updated ones

subjectOf.text: On-chain governance systems outperform traditional governance models in responsiveness only if they incorporate robust anti-collusion measures, a requirement SPoS meets through its cryptographic commitments.
subjectOf.abstract: Recent studies of on-chain governance in DAOs suggest that such systems can outperform traditional models in responsiveness, provided they incorporate robust anti-collusion measures—a challenge SPoS addresses through its cryptographic commitments
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Cryptographic Foundations and Interdisciplinary Dimensions of the Secure Proof of Stake (SPoS) Conse (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5225296
scope_conditions: requires robust anti-collusion measures to be in place
